clue.text: Money gets nails that's the nitty-gritty

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
tacks are small nails

explanation.surface: Someone notes that cash buys hardware, and that is the essential point.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting down to the basic facts of a matter is the idiom here; both phrases mean the core practical details.

clue.text: Composer dear to the Welsh

explanation.surface: A musician who is much loved in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian is the German composer; in Welsh, 'bach' is an affectionate form of address meaning little one or love.

clue.text: A flower found in Tuscany

parts.note: a flower is read as something that flows, a river, and the Tuscan one runs through Florence and Pisa

explanation.surface: A bloom growing wild in the Italian countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention reads 'flower' as a river; this one flows through Tuscany, past Florence and Pisa.

clue.text: Boost for gunman's victim?

explanation.surface: A fillip given by someone wounded by a shooter.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulating encouragement is the idiomatic sense; literally a gunman's victim might be hit by a bullet in a limb.

clue.text: Over to T E Lawrence

explanation.surface: A message handed to Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: T E Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under the name Ross, so he was Aircraftman (AC) Ross; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Over, as in from one side to the other, is a synonym; Lawrence served as Aircraftman Ross, abbreviated AC Ross.

clue.text: Amis was a Victorian novelist

explanation.surface: A claim that the twentieth-century writer Amis belonged to the nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley was the first name of the writer Amis and the surname of Charles, who wrote The Water-Babies.

clue.text: Dreary poet in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for poet is read backwards

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A dull writer of verse who has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab and dreary are synonyms for dull and colourless.

clue.text: His coroner turned out to be a beast

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters of these words are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A coroner who was revealed to be a brute.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhino is a large horned animal, an example of a beast.

clue.text: Fashionable fellows take wine if hunting

parts.note: bloods is an old term for fashionable young men about town
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Smart young men drink wine while out hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting animals for sport is the classic example of this pastime.

clue.text: Criminal on excursion is marking natural features

parts.note: a con, short for convict, is a criminal
touring is being on an excursion or trip

explanation.surface: A crook on a trip is noting landmarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing contour lines on a map records hills and valleys, the natural features of land.

clue.text: In Amalfi no-one serves dry sherry

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Nobody in the Italian coastal town offers a sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Fino is a pale, dry style of Spanish sherry.

clue.text: Brilliant coup gives teacher apoplexy

parts.note: a schoolmaster, master for short, is a teacher
apoplexy is an old medical word for a stroke

explanation.surface: A triumph causes a schoolteacher to have a seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke of genius, a brilliant move, is what the phrase means.

clue.text: If last orders change, see old service chief

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of these letters

explanation.surface: A pub-goer told about last orders goes to see a retired naval commander.
explanation.definitionFit: The professional head of the Royal Navy holds this title, a senior armed-forces commander.

clue.text: Fruit served by sergeant in mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Oranges dished out by a sergeant in the military dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small citrus fruits like mandarins.

clue.text: Soldiers needing respect have to think again

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
to consider someone is to respect or regard them

explanation.surface: Troops who want respect must rethink their approach.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to review a decision, to think it over afresh.

clue.text: Greeting holy man with a collection of sacred writings

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail
St, saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: Welcoming a priest who carries a bundle of scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the scripture of Zoroastrianism, a body of religious texts.

clue.text: Pay to live in a penthouse?

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether rent buys a top-floor flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a bill is the plain sense; literally, a penthouse resident makes a home high above.

clue.text: Contemplate spouse about to make textual changes

indicators.note: about means around, so one word is placed round the other

parts.note: a mate is a spouse or partner
to edit is to revise a text

explanation.surface: A husband or wife is about to revise a manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to think deeply and reflectively.

clue.text: Looked furious when note was reduced in pitch

parts.note: G is a musical note
lowered means brought down, as a pitch is

explanation.surface: Someone scowled when a musical note was flattened.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower is to scowl angrily.

clue.text: A redhead of sullen disposition exhibits zeal

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of red is R
dour describes a gloomy, sullen temperament

explanation.surface: A grumpy ginger-haired person shows unexpected enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is passion and enthusiasm, a synonym for fervour.

clue.text: About to ring the changes and get annulment

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a peal is a set of changes rung on bells

explanation.surface: Someone is about to change things and get a cancellation.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeal is the revoking of a law, a cancellation.

clue.text: Rome's rioting resulted in Italian liberation

indicators.note: resulted in says these letters have been turned into something new

parts.note: the words are taken with their letters as printed, including the S

explanation.surface: Unrest in Rome led to Italy being freed.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineteenth-century movement for the unification and independence of Italy is the historic reference.

clue.text: Sore cheek

explanation.surface: A painful spot on a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A gall is a sore made by rubbing; gall also means impudence.

clue.text: Accustomed to being exploited

explanation.surface: Someone is getting used to being taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: Used to means familiar with; used also means taken advantage of.

clue.text: Is leaving undies off and the rest!

definitions.text: Is leaving undies off and the rest!

indicators.note: off means altered, so the letters are rearranged once the other word's are removed

explanation.surface: Someone strips their underwear and everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' says the letters of IS come out of UNDIES; 'off' scrambles the rest, UND, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off underwear and all else leaves one naked, unclothed.

clue.text: Happened to have reached a defile

explanation.surface: Something occurred to travellers arriving at a mountain gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: Came to pass is an old idiom for occurred; a defile is a narrow mountain pass someone arrived at.

clue.text: Small animal shelter in the Channel Islands

parts.note: Noah's ark sheltered the animals

explanation.surface: A tiny refuge for animals on an island off France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is one of the smaller Channel Islands, a British dependency near Guernsey.

clue.text: We shall get listed as wealthy

parts.note: we'll is the contraction of we shall
a ship that heeled has listed, leaned to one side

explanation.surface: We will be recorded as rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-heeled is an idiom for rich or affluent.
